body:
As a workaround, I've written this tool script to add a Polygon2D child to CollisionPolygon2D nodes.
However I'm not sure how to get the multiple colors drawn for a single shape like they are in the editor.
I've been fiddling around with it for a bit, but I have no idea how it works. (If someone does know, that would be interesting just for my own curiosity...)

```gdscript
@tool
class_name PolyShader
extends CollisionPolygon2D

# Color palette for the triangles
@export var color_palette: Array = [
    Color(1, 0, 0, 0.5),  # Red
    Color(0, 1, 0, 0.5),  # Green
    Color(0, 0, 1, 0.5),  # Blue
    Color(1, 1, 0, 0.5),  # Yellow
    Color(1, 0, 1, 0.5)   # Magenta
]

# Tool button
@export var generate_polygon_button: bool = false:
    set(value):
        _generate_polygon_button_pressed()
        #if generate_polygon_button != value:
            #generate_polygon_button = value
            #print(generate_polygon_button)
    get:
        return generate_polygon_button

# Called when the button is clicked
func _generate_polygon_button_pressed():
    regenerate_polygon()

                
# Regenerate the Polygon2D based on the CollisionPolygon2D's polygon
func regenerate_polygon():
    # Search for a child of type Polygon2D
    var polygon2d_node = null
    for child in get_children():
        if child is Polygon2D:
            polygon2d_node = child
            break
    # If no Polygon2D node exists, create one
    if polygon2d_node == null:
        polygon2d_node = Polygon2D.new()
        self.add_child(polygon2d_node)
        polygon2d_node.owner = get_tree().edited_scene_root
    
    # Update Polygon2D
    polygon2d_node.polygon = self.polygon
    polygon2d_node.set_name("Polygon2D")
    polygon2d_node.color = color_palette[randi_range(0, color_palette.size()-1)]
```

The editor debug and the runtime are not the same mostly for performance and visual clutter reasons and because physics has no editor customization settings for that.

The polygon face drawing requires a convex decomposition. You can't draw those polygon outlines directly except for their lines so you need to turn them into convex polygons / triangles first. Depending on the complexity of the polygon outline this can be performance costly in a draw function at runtime.

What the debug does extra in the editor is to decompose convex the entire polygon array with `Geometry2D.decompose_polygon_in_convex()` into an array with convex polygons and then draw a rendering polygon for every single convex polygon with `CanvasItem.draw_colored_polygon()` using some semi random color. The code for that already exists but is disabled without editor tooling, aka at runtime.

Thank you. Convex decomposition, very interesting... I don't know if that existing code is written in C or GDScript, but I went ahead and took a crack at my own version. It's not perfect but I think it does a pretty good job of copying the behavior of the debug shapes.

Updated code is below if anyone is interested. Still not sure exactly how the colors are picked, but I just made a palette that cycles through. Thanks!



```gdscript
@tool
class_name PolyShader
extends CollisionPolygon2D

# Blend Mode
# Debug collision polygons do not appear to use regular alpha mix blend mode
# So we apply this CanvasItemMaterial with blend_mode = Premult Alpha
# And assign polygon color alpha of 0.5 to match the appearance of the debug shapes
const PREMULT_BLEND = preload("res://premult_blend.tres")

# alpha
@export_range (0, 1)
var alpha: float = 0.5

# options
@export var draw_convex = true  # draw convex polygons
@export var draw_solid = false  # draw a single solid colored polygon instead of convex polygons

# Tool button: press to test script in editor and generate polygons
@export var generate_polygon_button: bool = false:
	set(value):
		_generate_polygon_button_pressed()
	get:
		return generate_polygon_button
	

# Color palette for convex polygons
# To get these colors you can draw a CollisionPolygon2D over a Black background (ColorRect) in the editor
# Then use a color picker software to get the RGB / Hex color
# To determine the blending mode and alpha I checked the color against both black and white backgrounds
@export var convex_color_palette: Array[Color] = [
	Color("#73120d"),
	Color("#3e0d73"),
	Color("#0d7369"),
	Color("#50730d"),
	Color("#730d25"),
	Color("#200d73"),
	Color("#0d734c"),
	Color("#6e730d"),
	Color("#730d42"),
]


# Color palette for solids
@export var solid_color_palette: Array[Color] = [
	Color(1, 0, 0, 0.5),  # Red
	Color(0, 1, 0, 0.5),  # Green
	Color(0, 0, 1, 0.5),  # Blue
	Color(1, 1, 0, 0.5),  # Yellow
	Color(1, 0, 1, 0.5),   # Magenta
]
	
	
# Called when the button is clicked
func _generate_polygon_button_pressed():
	regenerate_polygon(self.polygon)


# Regenerate the Polygon2D based on the CollisionPolygon2D's polygon
func regenerate_polygon(polygon_points: Array):
	draw_solid_polygons(polygon_points)
	draw_convex_polygons(polygon_points)


# Draw a solid polygon
func draw_solid_polygons(polygon_points: Array):
	# Search for a child of type Polygon2D
	var polygon2d_node = null
	for child in get_children():
		if child is Polygon2D:
			polygon2d_node = child
			break
	# If no Polygon2D node exists, create one
	if polygon2d_node == null:
		polygon2d_node = Polygon2D.new()
		self.add_child(polygon2d_node)
		
		# Set owner in the editor, so we can see it update in the scene tree
		if Engine.is_editor_hint() and get_tree().edited_scene_root != null:
			polygon2d_node.owner = get_tree().edited_scene_root
	
	# Update Polygon2D
	polygon2d_node.polygon = polygon_points
	polygon2d_node.set_name("Polygon2D")
	polygon2d_node.color = solid_color_palette[randi_range(0, solid_color_palette.size()-1)]
	
	# Only show convex polygons; hide the base collision shape with modulate
	self.self_modulate.a = 1  # actually this messes up the colors if you make it 0 so leave it at 1
	
	# Visibility
	if !draw_solid:
		polygon2d_node.hide()
	else:
		polygon2d_node.show()
	
	
# Function to handle drawing of colored convex polygons
func draw_convex_polygons(polygon_points: Array):
	# Remove any existing polygons
	for child in self.get_children():
		if child.name.begins_with("convex"):
			child.queue_free()
		
	# Only draw polygons
	if polygon_points.size() < 3:
		print("Polygon must have at least 3 points.")
		return
	
	# Decompose the polygon into convex polygons
	var convex_polygons : Array[PackedVector2Array] = Geometry2D.decompose_polygon_in_convex(polygon_points)
	if convex_polygons.size() == 0:
		print("Failed to decompose polygon into convex parts.")
		return

	# Draw each convex polygon with a color from the color palette
	var i = 0
	for convex_polygon in convex_polygons:
		# Only draw closed polygon shapes
		if convex_polygon.size() < 3:
			continue

		# Choose a colors in order from the color palette
		var next_color : Color
		next_color = get_wrapped_color(i, convex_color_palette, alpha)

		# Add convex polygon
		var poly_child = Polygon2D.new()
		self.add_child(poly_child)
		
		# Set owner in the editor, so we can see it update in the scene tree
		if Engine.is_editor_hint() and get_tree().edited_scene_root != null:
			poly_child.owner = get_tree().edited_scene_root
		
		# Assign polygon and color
		poly_child.set_name("convex_polygon_%s" % str(i))
		poly_child.polygon = convex_polygon
		poly_child.color = next_color
		
		# Set blending mode
		poly_child.material = PREMULT_BLEND
		
		# Visibility
		if !draw_convex:
			poly_child.hide()
		else:
			poly_child.show()

		# Inc counter
		i += 1


func rgba_to_hex(color: Color) -> String:
	# Convert each channel (R, G, B, A) to a two-character hexadecimal value
	var r = "%02x" % int(color.r * 255)
	var g = "%02x" % int(color.g * 255)
	var b = "%02x" % int(color.b * 255)
	var a = "%02x" % int(color.a * 255)
	
	# Concatenate to form the hexadecimal string
	return "#%s%s%s%s" % [r, g, b, a]
	
	
func get_wrapped_color(i: int, color_array: Array, color_alpha: float) -> Color:
	
	if color_array.size() == 0:
		return Color.WHITE  # Return a default color if the palette is empty

	# Get next wrapped color
	var index = i % color_array.size()
	var next_color : Color = color_array[index]
	next_color.a = color_alpha
	
	return next_color

```

Continuing this discussion:

There is already a property for CollisionShape2D in the Project Settings called ```draw_2d_outlines```.
This setting adds a more visible border to collision shape 2d.
It shows up in both the running game and exports when Visible Collision Shapes is enabled.

To handle the performance concerns, I'd suggest a new project setting like ```draw_2d_polygon_fill```.
This would solve the issue of visual mismatch between the running and exported game; while allowing users flexibility to use an outline-only mode if performance is a concern.

I would also recommend the 2d outline setting to be applied to collision polygons as well--right now the outline is barely visible.
